effect_modifiers.evidence: median split: effect difference (above minus at or below median) -4270 dollars, 95% bootstrap interval -7899 to -640; quartile means of the pseudo-outcome -392, 396, -4254, -4113

limited_overlap.description: applicants with prior_earnings of about 39870 or more have a cross-fitted enrolment probability below 0.05 (3147 of 12000 program-year applicants, enrolled share 0.009); the effect for them rests on few enrolled cases. 739 of 4000 new applicants fall in this region.

warnings: Response to the follow-up survey is modelled as missing at random given the covariates and enrolment. This cannot be checked with these data; if response depends on unmeasured earnings, the earnings effects are biased.

Enrolled share is 0.615 in the bottom quartile of prior_earnings and 0.009 in the top quartile; the adjusted effects depend on the no-unmeasured-confounding assumption. See sensitivity.json for a bias table.
Channel decomposition uses employment and earnings-among-employed models; the wage part is conditional on employment and is not a randomized comparison.
Intervals are normal approximations: estimate plus or minus 1.645 times the standard deviation over 18 bootstrap replicates of the full pipeline.
Effect-modifier claims are based on 95% bootstrap intervals of median-split contrasts, with no adjustment for the number of contrasts tested.
Covariate roles were assigned by a LightGBM drop-one screen with z threshold 2.0; instrument status is a rule (enrolment z at least 4.0), not a test of the exclusion restriction.

Instrumental-variable check with distance_km: beta 4567 dollars per unit of enrolment, first-stage partial correlation -0.138; this estimate applies to applicants whose enrolment responds to distance.
The bootstrap stopped after 18 of 30 replicates to stay within the time budget.
